questions.question: Which set is bounded?
options: $\{x\in\mathbb{Q}\colon |x| \le 3\}$
$\{x\in\mathbb{Q}\colon |x| \ge 3\}$
$\{x\in\mathbb{Q}\colon x \le 3\}$
$\{1/x\colon x\in\mathbb{Q},\ 0<x\le 3\}$

questions.question: Which set is not bounded?
options: $\mathbb{N}$
$\{x\in\mathbb{Q}\colon |x| \le 3\}$

questions.question: What is true about bounded intervals?
options: Every bounded interval is a bounded set
Only closed bounded intervals are bounded sets
Every bounded interval has a maximum element
A bounded interval may be infinitely long, like $[0,\infty)$

questions.question: Why is $\{1,2,3\}$ bounded?
options: It consists of natural numbers, which are bounded below
It is an interval with endpoints $1$ and $3$
It is finite, and every finite set is bounded
It has a largest element, which alone makes a set bounded

questions.question: Which $M$ shows that $[-2,5]$ is bounded using $[-M,M]$?
Why does the definition allow containment in $[-M,M]$ rather than requiring $X = [-M,M]$?
options: A bounded set must equal an interval, though not necessarily a symmetric one
With equality, only finite sets could be bounded
A bounded set only needs to fit inside a bounded interval
A bounded set must contain $0$, the centre of $[-M,M]$

questions.question: Which statement correctly connects bounded sets and bounded intervals?
options: Every bounded set is a bounded interval, and conversely.
A set is bounded only if it lies in the fixed interval $[-1,1]$.
Bounded intervals are bounded sets, but bounded sets need not lie in one.
Bounded sets lie in bounded intervals, and vice versa.

questions.question: Which set is bounded but is not itself an interval?
options: $\mathbb{N}$
$\mathbb{R}$
$\{x\in\mathbb{R}\colon x \ge 0\}$

questions.question: If $X\subseteq[-4,4]$, what follows directly from the definition?
options: $X$ is unbounded
$X$ is bounded
$X = \mathbb{R}$
$X$ must be finite

questions.question: A set of real numbers is bounded above. Which additional condition makes the set bounded?
options: bounded below
infinite
a closed interval
non-empty

questions.question: If $X$ is bounded and $Y\subseteq X$, is $Y$ bounded?
options: Yes; subsets inherit the bound
No; subsets can be unbounded
Only if $Y$ is finite or an interval
Yes, but only with a strictly smaller $M$

questions.question: What is an unbounded set?
options: A set not contained in the interval $[-1,1]$.
A set containing infinitely many real numbers.
A set not contained in any bounded interval.
A set that has no largest element.

questions.question: Which quantities are guaranteed to exist for a nonempty bounded set of real numbers?
options: both a supremum and an infimum
a maximum and a minimum
a supremum but possibly no infimum
a supremum lying in the set

questions.question: If $A$ and $B$ are bounded sets, is $A\cup B$ bounded?
options: Yes; their union is bounded
No; a union is never bounded
Only when the sets are disjoint
Only when both sets are identical

questions.question: Is the open interval $(0,1)$ a bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}$?
options: It is bounded, for example by $M=1$.
It is unbounded because it is open.
It is unbounded because it has infinitely many elements.
It is bounded only if it contains its endpoints.

questions.question: What is the geometric interpretation of a bounded set in $\mathbb{R}$?
options: All elements lie within one finite distance of $0$.
Each element lies at a finite distance from $0$.
The set covers only a finite total length of the line.
The set is centred at $0$, symmetric about the origin.

questions.question: Let $X=\{x\in\mathbb{R}\colon |x| \lt 5\}$. Which statement is correct?
options: $X$ is unbounded because it is open.
$X$ is unbounded because it has infinitely many elements.
$X$ is bounded only if $5\in X$.
$X$ is bounded because $X\subseteq[-5,5]$.
